items.title: Quick Flows (Turn repeated work into a fixed set of steps) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 10
items.summary: Level 200. A handout on AWS Quick Flows, for people who use AWS Quick at work and ask it for the same thing again and again. It covers what Quick Flows is (steps you decide once and run any time, and how it differs from routines and Quick Automate); building a flow (describing it in words to get a draft, the five kinds of steps, a flow that turns meeting notes into key points and action items, and fixing a step prompt with @ references); and running and keeping it (Run mode, downloading the answers as PDF or Word or saving them to a space, schedule triggers, versions, sharing and approval review, and the limits). The screenshots show the web app with the English display language. The running example, a monthly internal learning session, is fictional. The appendix has the kinds of steps, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 10 (Let it run) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: Quick on the web (Use chat, spaces, and agents in your browser) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 02
items.summary: Level 100. A handout for anyone who uses AWS Quick on the web, in a browser. The web screen and signing in: the left menu, the chat box on Home, the two ways to sign in (an aws.com/quick account or a company account), and the two chat modes (collapse and expand). Asking in chat, with a running example of organizing a monthly internal learning session: choosing the built-in agent or an agent someone made, the three data scopes (General knowledge, All data, and Specific data), turning web search off for a request, and attaching files. Keeping the results: the artifact panel and its download formats, chat history for up to 90 days, Private Mode for chats you don't want kept, and memory. From chat to other features: asking in a space, switching to an agent with its own knowledge, running a flow, and starting Quick Research. What the web doesn't do: the browser and Microsoft 365 extensions, and the features that are only in the desktop app or the mobile app. Screens of the web app in English show each step. The appendix has chat and space limits, terms and screen names, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 02 (Get started) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: Connectors and extensions (Connect your business apps and MCP servers) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 07
items.summary: Level 200. A handout on connecting AWS Quick to the business apps you already use, for people who connect apps and the admins who allow it. It covers four ways to connect (knowledge bases, connectors, extensions, and data sources); connectors (adding one from the Available tab, creating one for your team, signing in with the Default OAuth app, a custom OAuth app, service-to-service OAuth, or an API key, and using connector tools in chat); tool permissions (Let Users Choose, Always Ask, and Disable for the owner, Always Allow, Always Ask, and Disable for each user, and the defaults for read and write tools); your own tools (remote MCP servers over the public network or through a VPC connection, OpenAPI specs, and REST APIs, plus local MCP servers and coding agents in the desktop app); and extensions (the browser extension, the Microsoft 365 add-ins for Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, and Slack and Microsoft Teams). The running example collects attendance replies for a learning session with the Outlook connector. The screens were taken on the web in English. The appendix lists the services you can connect, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 07 (Go deeper) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.
